# Problem setup:

## Points

- A(-2.0081, -1.4301)
- B(0.2739, -0.4604)
- C(0.0976, -1.9013)
- E(-0.6800, -1.7273)
- M(-0.9181, -0.9669)
- N(0.2415, -0.7257)
- O(-0.8192, -1.0579)

## Assumptions:

[C0] : O is the circumcenter of the circle ●ABC
[C1] : EN = AE
[C2] : EM = CE
[C3] : ∠(BM,BN) = 1pi/3
[C4] : AM = MN
[C5] : CN = MN
[C6] : AN ⟂ EM
[C7] : CM ⟂ EN

## Numerical checks

[N0] : A, B, O are not collinear
[N1] : A, E, N are not collinear
[N2] : C, E, M are not collinear
[N3] : A, M, N are not collinear
[N4] : C, M, N are not collinear
[N5] : B, C, O are not collinear


# Goals

A, N, O are collinear : Proved [16]
C, M, O are collinear : Proved [20]


# Proof:

000. | O is the circumcenter of the circle ●ABC [C0] =(r72 Disassembling a circle)> BO = AO [0]
001. | BO = AO [0], A, B, O are not collinear [N0] =(r13 Isosceles triangle equal angles)> ∠(AB,AO) = ∠(BO,AB) [1]
002. | EN = AE [C1], A, E, N are not collinear [N1] =(r13 Isosceles triangle equal angles)> ∠(AE,AN) = ∠(AN,EN) [2]
003. | EM = CE [C2], C, E, M are not collinear [N2] =(r13 Isosceles triangle equal angles)> ∠(CE,CM) = ∠(CM,EM) [3]
004. | ∠(AE,AN) = ∠(AN,EN) [2], ∠(CE,CM) = ∠(CM,EM) [3] =(AR Deduction)> AE ∥ CE [4]
005. | AE ∥ CE [4] =(r28 Overlapping parallels)> A, C, E are collinear [5]
006. | A, C, E are collinear [5] =(r82 Parallel from collinear)> AC ∥ AE [6]
007. | AM = MN [C4], A, M, N are not collinear [N3] =(r13 Isosceles triangle equal angles)> ∠(AM,AN) = ∠(AN,MN) [7]
008. | ∠(BM,BN) = 1pi/3 [C3], ∠(AM,AN) = ∠(AN,MN) [7] =(AR Deduction)> AM ∥ BM [8]
009. | AM ∥ BM [8] =(r28 Overlapping parallels)> A, B, M are collinear [9]
010. | A, B, M are collinear [9] =(r82 Parallel from collinear)> AM ∥ AB [10]
011. | CN = MN [C5], C, M, N are not collinear [N4] =(r13 Isosceles triangle equal angles)> ∠(CM,CN) = ∠(MN,CM) [11]
012. | ∠(CM,CN) = ∠(MN,CM) [11] =(AR Deduction)> CN ∥ BN [12]
013. | CN ∥ BN [12] =(r28 Overlapping parallels)> B, C, N are collinear [13]
014. | B, C, N are collinear [13] =(r82 Parallel from collinear)> BN ∥ BC [14]
015. | ∠(AB,AO) = ∠(BO,AB) [1], AC ∥ AE [6], AM ∥ AB [10], BN ∥ BC [14], AN ⟂ EM [C6] =(AR Deduction)> AN ∥ AO [15]
016. | AN ∥ AO [15] =(r28 Overlapping parallels)> A, N, O are collinear [16]
017. | O is the circumcenter of the circle ●ABC [C0] =(r72 Disassembling a circle)> CO = BO [17]
018. | CO = BO [17], B, C, O are not collinear [N5] =(r13 Isosceles triangle equal angles)> ∠(BC,BO) = ∠(CO,BC) [18]
019. | ∠(BC,BO) = ∠(CO,BC) [18], AC ∥ AE [6], BN ∥ BC [14], CM ⟂ EN [C7] =(AR Deduction)> CO ∥ CM [19]
020. | CO ∥ CM [19] =(r28 Overlapping parallels)> C, M, O are collinear [20]


# Appendix: AR deductions:



004. | Angle Chasing to prove AE ∥ CE:
| Premise ∠(AE,AN) = ∠(AN,EN) gives a linear equation with coefficients {}
| Premise ∠(CE,CM) = ∠(CM,EM) gives a linear equation with coefficients {}
We are left with a linear equation with coefficients {} that gives AE ∥ CE



008. | Angle Chasing to prove AM ∥ BM:
| Premise ∠(BM,BN) = 1pi/3 gives a linear equation with coefficients {}
| Premise ∠(AM,AN) = ∠(AN,MN) gives a linear equation with coefficients {}
We are left with a linear equation with coefficients {} that gives AM ∥ BM



012. | Angle Chasing to prove CN ∥ BN:
| Premise ∠(CM,CN) = ∠(MN,CM) gives a linear equation with coefficients {}
We are left with a linear equation with coefficients {} that gives CN ∥ BN



015. | Angle Chasing to prove AN ∥ AO:
| Premise ∠(AB,AO) = ∠(BO,AB) gives a linear equation with coefficients {}
| Premise AC ∥ AE gives a linear equation with coefficients {}
| Premise AM ∥ AB gives a linear equation with coefficients {}
| Premise BN ∥ BC gives a linear equation with coefficients {}
| Premise AN ⟂ EM gives a linear equation with coefficients {}
We are left with a linear equation with coefficients {} that gives AN ∥ AO



019. | Angle Chasing to prove CO ∥ CM:
| Premise ∠(BC,BO) = ∠(CO,BC) gives a linear equation with coefficients {}
| Premise AC ∥ AE gives a linear equation with coefficients {}
| Premise BN ∥ BC gives a linear equation with coefficients {}
| Premise CM ⟂ EN gives a linear equation with coefficients {}
We are left with a linear equation with coefficients {} that gives CO ∥ CM

End of proof.
